method_notes: **Before calling anything a gate, find the line that refuses.** Five conclusions lost their consequence half this cycle. Procedure: `git grep` the symbol at the pinned rev, list EVERY consumer, and classify each as compute / serialize / render / print / refuse. If nothing is in the last bucket, it is decoration -- say so in the report rather than being told.

**Never hand-type a timestamp.** I did it four times in filenames and heartbeats while auditing that exact defect class. One command: `python -c "import datetime;print(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))"`.

**Cite `<rev>:<file>:<line>`, never bare `<file>:<line>`, for append-only files.** Every append shifts them. I got PARTNER_SYNC:1554 wrong in the same cycle I criticised someone else for the identical error.

**Live state vs tracked state**: board.log, board/items|claimed|done, ops-status, logs, locks, quota/accounts -- the WORKING TREE is authoritative and lags git by hours in BOTH directions. Code -- git at a pinned rev is authoritative. Reading tracked board state cost me a whole finding this cycle.
**Check the base rate before calling an instance a deviation.** 'RES-4 left two files untracked' looked like drift until the count came back 76 of 160 untracked, 70 of them same-day.

**Never diff a manifest against HEAD.** Recover its declared base; failing that, replay its hashes across candidate revs and take the best fit. If no base is recoverable, THAT missing field is the finding, and it is far smaller than the mismatch count.

**`core.autocrlf` is true here.** Any hash from `open(path,'rb')` is a CRLF hash and can never equal `git cat-file blob` for text files without an `eol` attribute. ~1 in 7 text files mints a phantom mismatch.
**Purge `__pycache__` between mutants.** Equal-length edits within the same mtime second reuse stale bytecode and manufacture false survivors.

**Mutation recipe, corrected**: `git archive <rev> proxy arc-recon/data | tar -x -C $TEMP/x && cd $TEMP/x && git init -q . && git add . && git commit -qm base`. A bare `mkdir .git` is NOT enough -- `test_chain.py` shells out to `git check-ignore`. For `monitor/`, prefer a real `git clone` of the repo: the archive lacks PARTNER_SYNC.md and other territories' runs/, which produces two false reds and, in my case, made a production count of 18 look like 1.
**Point `scan.ROOT` at the real tree (read-only) rather than at an archive** when measuring what a probe actually reports. The repo's own tests do exactly this (`test_probes_injection.py:34`).

**A registered residual with a stated 'no executable form' is a documented limitation, not drift** -- and so is a limitation the author self-disclosed in an append-only mainline document. Search RESIDUALS/RULING/OPEN_ITEMS/DECISIONS *and* the author's own PARTNER_SYNC paragraph before filing.

self_correction_rule: Before reporting 'X is missing / X is broken / X never ran', spend one command proving you are not looking at yourself, at a second copy elsewhere, at a path that never executes, at a gate belonging to a different phase, at a stale local checkout while the mainline moved on, at a trace the code was never going to leave, at a claim your own lineage already killed, at a limitation already registered in RESIDUALS/RULING/OPEN_ITEMS/DECISIONS **or self-disclosed by the author in an append-only document**, at a verdict phrase you have mistaken for a component name, **at TRACKED state when the question is about LIVE state**, or **at an instance whose base rate you have not measured**. Cycle 43's amendment stands (the checklist is not a substitute for a refuter -- it passed all four conclusions the refuters went on to kill). **Cycle 44's amendment: the checklist does not catch the consequence error either. Only 'find the line that refuses' catches that one, and it must be a separate, deliberate step.**

handoff.first thing to do: Read your own launch words. 60 minutes in the prompt = headless dispatch (cycle 40's discriminator, now confirmed five times); 30 = a human pasted the contract. Mine said 60 and `standing.log` showed `START OPS-A (lane=None) ok=True` at 22:46:33Z, ~1 min before my first tool call -- consistent.
handoff.second thing to do: `git fetch && git rev-parse origin/master` and compare to HEAD. **Do not assume the lag direction** -- it is sawtooth, not monotone (see THE_SECOND_BIG_FACT). Then fan out 5-6 gatherers pinned to ONE rev and budget one refuter per conclusion.
